US inflation is diverging from the Fed’s target:

US CPI Inflation has surged +30.2% since January 2020, to an all-time high.

This translates into an annualized inflation rate of +4.0% over this period.

Meanwhile, under a steady 2% annual inflation target, cumulative CPI growth would have been just +14.3%.

In other words, actual cumulative inflation is +15.9 percentage points above the target path, more than double the implied increase.

This comes as CPI has remained above 2% for 67 consecutive months.

The gap began widening again in March, as inflation has now remained above 3% for 7 consecutive months.

CHART OF THE DAY: While the surge in Saudi oil production in October attracted most of the attention, there was another big jump: Iraq. 

Baghdad boosted output to a 7-year high of ~4.6m b/d last month (just under the all-time high of ~4.8m b/d of Aug 2019) exporting crude via Strait of Hormuz, but also pipeline (via Turkey) and trucking (via Syria) to Mediterranean Sea. 

Iraqi oil production has not only  recovered well above pre-war levels, but the country has much bigger plans. 

Last month, I wrote an @Opinion column flagging how Iraq is attracting international oil companies and could emerge from the war stronger: 

"Yes, Iraq is a risky destination, even more so today with a war raging in the neighborhood. But for the first time in decades, the country offers Big Oil the kind of returns it aspires to."

$QQQ gamma map is set up for downside and it's not even close

Quick explainer for anyone who hasn't seen one of these. This is a GEX heatmap. It basically shows where dealers are stuck hedging at each strike.

Green/yellow = positive gamma. Dealers buy dips, sell rips there. Price gets pinned, moves slow down.
Dark/purple = negative gamma. Dealers have to sell as price falls. No cushion. Moves get fast and ugly.

Now look at the actual numbers on this map

Below price: -$3.9B
Above price: +$1.8B

That's the whole story. More than 2x the pressure below us than above us.

Above, 685-690 is stacked green. That's why every single bounce this week got sold right there. It's a wall.

Below is where it gets interesting. The nodes just keep getting darker the lower you go. 682, 667, 659, 655... and then there's the 650 strike for Nov 20 expiry sitting at like -$1.6B. That one node is massive.

If 660 goes and 647 (November low) breaks, dealers hedging that book aren't catching the knife, they're selling into it. 650 becomes a magnet. And 650 is basically the doorway to the 620-630 January shelf I've been talking about all week.

Honest part though, because I don't want anyone treating this like gospel

This map redraws every day. Nodes change as positions open and close. This is Friday's map. Monday's could look different. It backs up the levels, it doesn't replace them. Close above 685 and I'm redrawing everything.

And there's two headlines this week that can blow this whole setup up

1. The "Stand with Jensen" petition. 43K+ signatures, thousands of actual Nvidia employees, Musk signed it, big shareholders are literally writing the board telling them to keep his return on the table. Jensen comes back = NVDA squeeze = QQQ drop scenario probably gets delayed.

2. NVDA earnings Tuesday. Clean beat, good guidance, this gets delayed again. Simple as that.

So yeah. Trap confirmed Friday, path is 660 → 647 → 650 node → 620s. But I'm not marrying it. Two binary headlines this week can flip it in a day.

Day by day. Levels first.
